pyq.answer: b
pyq.solution: Differentiated parenchyma regaining the capacity to divide is dedifferentiation; the secondary tissues they later produce are redifferentiated.

pyq.q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
pyq.answer: b
pyq.solution: Cytokinins promote nutrient mobilisation and delay leaf senescence. ABA inhibits germination, auxin (not ethylene) causes apical dominance, and ABA (not auxin) closes stomata.

pyq.q: Assertion (A): Abscisic acid is called the stress hormone. Reason (R): ABA stimulates closure of stomata and increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
pyq.answer: a
pyq.solution: Both statements are NCERT sentences and the reason is exactly why ABA earns the name stress hormone.

pyq.q: Assertion (A): Growth in plants is indeterminate. Reason (R): Plants possess meristems at certain locations whose cells retain the capacity to divide and self-perpetuate.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
pyq.answer: a
pyq.solution: Meristems keep adding new cells throughout life, which is what makes plant growth indeterminate and open.

pyq.q: Assertion (A): Removal of the shoot tip of a plant usually results in the growth of lateral buds. Reason (R): Cytokinin produced by the shoot apex inhibits the lateral buds.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
pyq.answer: c
pyq.solution: Decapitation does release the lateral buds (A true), but it is auxin from the apex that inhibits them; cytokinin actually helps overcome apical dominance (R false).

pyq.q: Assertion (A): Two leaves that increase in area by the same amount in the same time need not have the same relative growth rate. Reason (R): Relative growth rate is expressed per unit initial size, so the smaller leaf shows the higher relative growth.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
pyq.answer: a
pyq.solution: Leaf A (5 to 10 cm<sup>2</sup>) and leaf B (50 to 55 cm<sup>2</sup>) both add 5 cm<sup>2</sup>, yet their relative growth is 100 per cent and 10 per cent respectively.

pyq.q: Differentiate between arithmetic growth and geometric growth (two points).
pyq.answer: (i) In arithmetic growth only one daughter cell of a mitotic division continues to divide while the other differentiates; in geometric growth both daughter cells retain the ability to divide. (ii) Arithmetic growth adds a constant amount per unit time and gives a straight-line graph, Lt = L0 + rt; geometric growth is exponential and gives a sigmoid curve with lag, log and stationary phases, W1 = W0ert.

pyq.q: What is plasticity in plants? Give one example.
pyq.answer: Plasticity is the ability of plants to follow different pathways in response to the environment or to phases of life to form different kinds of structures. Example: heterophylly in cotton, coriander and larkspur, where the leaves of the juvenile plant differ in shape from those of the mature plant; or buttercup, where leaves formed in air differ in shape from those formed in water.

pyq.q: Name the plant growth regulator you would use to (a) obtain seedless tomatoes and (b) hasten the ripening of a consignment of bananas. Name the compound commercially used as a source of the second one.
pyq.answer: (a) Auxin, which induces parthenocarpy in tomatoes. (b) Ethylene, which is highly effective in fruit ripening. The compound used commercially as a source of ethylene is ethephon, which is absorbed in aqueous solution and releases ethylene slowly.

pyq.q: Name the three phases of growth at a root tip in the order in which they occur from the apex, and state one feature of the cells in the phase of elongation.
pyq.answer: From the apex backwards: meristematic phase (zone of cell division), phase of elongation and phase of maturation. Cells in the phase of elongation show increased vacuolation, cell enlargement and new cell wall deposition.

pyq.q: Why is it that a lawn treated with 2,4-D becomes free of broad-leaved weeds while the grass survives?
pyq.answer: 2,4-D is a synthetic auxin used as a herbicide. It kills dicotyledonous (broad-leaved) weeds but does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants; grass is a monocot, so it survives while the dicot weeds die, giving a weed-free lawn.

pyq.q: Describe the discovery of auxin, naming the scientists and the plant material used.
pyq.answer: Charles Darwin and his son Francis Darwin observed that the coleoptiles of canary grass grew towards a unilateral light source (phototropism). From a series of experiments (removing the tip, covering the tip, covering the base) they concluded that the tip of the coleoptile was the site of a transmittable influence that caused the bending of the entire coleoptile. Later F.W. Went isolated this substance, auxin, from the tips of coleoptiles of oat seedlings: tips placed on agar blocks passed the substance into the agar, and an agar block placed on one side of a decapitated coleoptile made it bend, showing a diffusible chemical was responsible. The name comes from the Greek 'auxein', to grow. Auxin was first isolated from human urine.

pyq.q: What are the conditions necessary for plant growth? Explain the role of each.
pyq.answer: (i) Water: cells grow by enlargement, which requires water; turgidity of cells helps in extension growth, and water is the medium for enzymatic activities needed for growth. (ii) Oxygen: it helps in releasing metabolic energy through respiration, which is essential for growth activities. (iii) Nutrients: macro- and micro-elements are required for the synthesis of protoplasm and act as a source of energy. (iv) Optimum temperature: every plant grows only within a suitable range of temperature; deviation may be detrimental to survival. (v) Light and gravity: these environmental signals affect certain phases or stages of growth, for example phototropism and geotropism.

pyq.q: Explain dedifferentiation and redifferentiation with examples. Why is differentiation in plants said to be open?
pyq.answer: Dedifferentiation: living differentiated cells that have lost the capacity to divide regain it under certain conditions; for example, fully differentiated parenchyma cells form the interfascicular cambium and the cork cambium during secondary growth. Redifferentiation: the dedifferentiated cells divide and produce cells that again lose the capacity to divide and mature to perform specific functions; for example, secondary xylem and secondary phloem produced by the interfascicular cambium, and cork produced by the cork cambium. Differentiation is open because cells arising from the same meristem have different structures at maturity, the final structure being decided by the position of the cell in the organ: cells away from the root apical meristem become root cap, cells pushed to the periphery become epidermis.

pyq.q: Give three physiological effects of gibberellins and one agricultural use of each.
pyq.answer: (i) They increase the length of the axis: used to lengthen grape stalks so that the bunches are looser and the berries larger, and to increase the stem length of sugarcane, raising yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre. (ii) They delay senescence: fruits such as apples can be left on the tree longer, extending the market period; GA also makes apples elongate and improve in shape. (iii) They promote bolting (internode elongation before flowering) in rosette plants like beet and cabbage, and hasten maturity in juvenile conifers, leading to early seed production. In addition GA3 is used to speed up malting in the brewing industry.

pyq.q: State the chemical nature of the five groups of plant growth regulators with one example of each, and classify them into growth promoters and growth inhibitors.
pyq.answer: Auxins are indole compounds (indole-3-acetic acid, IAA); cytokinins are adenine derivatives (kinetin, N6-furfurylamino purine; zeatin); gibberellins are terpenes (gibberellic acid, GA3); abscisic acid is a derivative of carotenoids; ethylene is a gas (C2H4). Auxins, gibberellins and cytokinins are growth promoters, involved in cell division, cell enlargement, pattern formation, tropic growth, flowering, fruiting and seed formation. ABA is a growth inhibitor, involved in dormancy, abscission and responses to wounds and stress. Ethylene could fit either group but is largely an inhibitor of growth activities.

pyq.q: Describe the physiological effects of ethylene on plants. Why is it called one of the most widely used plant growth regulators in agriculture?
pyq.answer:
Ethylene is a simple gaseous PGR synthesised in large amounts by tissues undergoing senescence and by ripening fruits. Its effects: (i) horizontal growth of seedlings, swelling of the axis and apical hook formation in dicot seedlings; (ii) promotion of senescence and abscission of plant organs, especially leaves and flowers; (iii) it is highly effective in fruit ripening and enhances the respiration rate during ripening, the respiratory climactic; (iv) it breaks seed and bud dormancy, initiates germination in peanut seeds and sprouting of potato tubers; (v) it promotes rapid internode and petiole elongation in deep-water rice, keeping the leaves above water; (vi) it promotes root growth and root hair formation, increasing the absorption surface.

Agricultural uses: ethylene is used to initiate flowering and to synchronise fruit-set in pineapples, and to induce flowering in mango. The most widely used source is ethephon, which in aqueous solution is readily absorbed and transported within the plant and releases ethylene slowly. Ethephon hastens fruit ripening in tomatoes and apples, accelerates abscission in flowers and fruits (thinning of cotton, cherry and walnut) and promotes female flowers in cucumbers, increasing yield. Because it regulates so many processes and can be applied cheaply as ethephon, ethylene is one of the most widely used PGRs in agriculture.

pyq.q: Explain arithmetic and geometric growth with equations and graphs. Describe the sigmoid growth curve and explain absolute and relative growth rates with an example.
pyq.answer:
Arithmetic growth: after mitosis only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures, so a constant amount is added per unit time. A root elongating at a constant rate is the simplest example. The graph of length against time is a straight line rising from L0; Lt = L0 + rt, where Lt is length at time t, L0 length at time zero and r the growth rate (elongation per unit time).

Geometric growth: both daughter cells retain the ability to divide, so the size multiplies. Growth is slow at first (lag phase), then exponential (log phase), then slows as nutrients become limiting (stationary phase). W1 = W0ert, where W1 is the final size, W0 the initial size, r the relative growth rate (also called the efficiency index), t the time and e the base of natural logarithms; the final size depends on the initial size.

Sigmoid curve: plotting the growth parameter against time for an organism in a natural environment gives an S-shaped curve made of the lag, exponential and stationary phases (draw and label it). It is typical for all cells, tissues and organs of a plant.

Absolute and relative growth rates: absolute growth rate is total growth per unit time; relative growth rate is growth per unit time per unit initial size. Two leaves that both add 5 cm2 in the same time have equal absolute growth; but leaf A, growing from 5 to 10 cm2, has a relative growth of 100 per cent while leaf B, growing from 50 to 55 cm2, has only 10 per cent.

pyq.q: Give an account of the physiological effects and applications of auxins and cytokinins, and explain how the two interact in apical dominance.
pyq.answer:
Auxins (natural IAA and IBA; synthetic NAA and 2,4-D) are produced by the growing apices of stems and roots and migrate to their sites of action. They initiate rooting in stem cuttings (used in propagation), promote flowering in pineapple, prevent fruit and leaf drop at early stages but promote abscission of older mature leaves and fruits, cause apical dominance, induce parthenocarpy (seedless tomatoes), control xylem differentiation and help in cell division. 2,4-D is widely used as a herbicide that kills dicot weeds without affecting mature monocots, giving weed-free lawns.

Cytokinins (kinetin, a modified adenine from herring sperm DNA; natural zeatin from corn kernels and coconut milk) are synthesised where cell division is rapid: root apices, developing shoot buds and young fruits. They help produce new leaves, chloroplasts in leaves, lateral shoot growth and adventitious shoots; they overcome apical dominance; and they promote nutrient mobilisation, which delays leaf senescence. In tissue culture they are needed with auxin for callus proliferation and shoot formation.

Interaction in apical dominance: auxin from the growing apical bud inhibits the lateral buds, so the plant grows tall with few branches. Removing the tip (decapitation) stops the auxin supply and the lateral buds grow, which is why tea bushes and hedges are pruned. Cytokinins act in the opposite direction, promoting lateral bud growth and so overcoming apical dominance; the auxin-to-cytokinin ratio decides whether the apex or the side buds grow.

pyq.q: Describe how each of the five groups of plant growth regulators was discovered.
pyq.answer: All five were discovered accidentally. Auxin: Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin found that coleoptiles of canary grass bend towards unilateral light and that the tip is the site of a transmittable influence; F.W. Went isolated auxin from oat coleoptile tips using agar blocks. Gibberellin: rice seedlings infected by the fungus Gibberella fujikuroi showed the bakanae (foolish seedling) disease, growing abnormally tall; E. Kurosawa reproduced the symptoms in uninfected seedlings with sterile filtrates of the fungus, and the active substance was later identified as gibberellic acid. Cytokinin: F. Skoog and co-workers found that callus from tobacco stem internodes proliferated only when the medium, besides auxin, contained extracts of vascular tissue, yeast extract, coconut milk or DNA; Skoog and Miller identified and crystallised the cytokinesis-promoting substance, kinetin, from autoclaved herring sperm DNA. Abscisic acid: in the mid-1960s three independent groups purified three inhibitors, inhibitor-B, abscission II and dormin, which were later shown to be chemically identical and named ABA. Ethylene: H.H. Cousins confirmed that ripened oranges released a volatile substance that hastened the ripening of stored unripe bananas; the substance was later identified as ethylene.

pyq.q:
A fruit vendor stores unripe bananas in a closed room. He notices that when a few ripe oranges are kept in the same room, the bananas ripen much faster; when a rotten mango is left in a basket of green mangoes, the whole basket spoils in two days. His neighbour, a farmer, sprays a chemical on his pineapple field so that all the plants flower and set fruit at the same time, and dips the cut ends of rose twigs in a powder before planting them.
(i) Name the plant growth regulator responsible for the faster ripening of bananas and the scientist who first confirmed this effect.
(ii) Why does one rotten mango spoil the whole basket?
(iii) Name the compound the farmer most probably sprays on pineapple and the PGR it releases.
(iv) Which PGR is in the rooting powder? Give one natural and one synthetic example.
pyq.answer:
(i) Ethylene, a gaseous PGR released by ripening fruits; H.H. Cousins confirmed that ripe oranges release a volatile substance that hastens ripening of bananas. (1 mark)

(ii) The rotten mango, a senescing and over-ripe tissue, produces ethylene in large amounts; being a gas it spreads through the basket and induces ripening and senescence (with a respiratory climactic) in the green mangoes, which then over-ripen and rot. (1 mark)

(iii) Ethephon, which is absorbed in aqueous solution and releases ethylene slowly; ethylene initiates flowering and synchronises fruit-set in pineapple. (1 mark)

(iv) Auxin, which initiates rooting in stem cuttings. Natural: IAA or IBA; synthetic: NAA or 2,4-D. (1 mark)

pyq.q:
A student measured the height of two seedlings, P and Q, every day for four days. P: 2 cm, 4 cm, 6 cm, 8 cm. Q: 2 cm, 4 cm, 8 cm, 16 cm. She also measured two leaves on a plant: leaf X grew from 4 cm2 to 8 cm2 and leaf Y from 20 cm2 to 24 cm2 in the same week.
(i) Which seedling shows arithmetic growth and which geometric? Give the reason at the cellular level.
(ii) Write the equation for the growth of seedling P and find its growth rate.
(iii) Which leaf has the higher absolute growth and which the higher relative growth? Show the calculation.
(iv) If seedling Q continued for many more days, what shape of curve would its growth eventually show and why?
pyq.answer:
(i) P shows arithmetic growth (a constant 2 cm is added each day); Q shows geometric growth (the height doubles each day). In arithmetic growth only one daughter cell of each division keeps dividing while the other differentiates; in geometric growth both daughter cells keep dividing. (1 mark)

(ii) Lt = L0 + rt. With L0 = 2 cm and Lt = 8 cm at t = 3 days, r = (8 − 2)/3 = 2 cm per day. (1 mark)

(iii) Absolute growth: X = 8 − 4 = 4 cm2; Y = 24 − 20 = 4 cm2; both equal. Relative growth: X = 4/4 = 100 per cent; Y = 4/20 = 20 per cent. Leaf X has the higher relative growth rate. (1 mark)

(iv) A sigmoid (S-shaped) curve: after the exponential (log) phase the growth would slow down and reach a stationary phase because the supply of nutrients becomes limiting, as happens for any organism growing in a natural environment. (1 mark)

practice_mcq.q: Which of the following is a natural cytokinin isolated from corn kernels and coconut milk?
practice_mcq.explanation: Zeatin is the natural cytokinin; kinetin is synthetic (from herring sperm DNA), IBA is an auxin and ethephon releases ethylene.

practice_mcq.q: Spraying sugarcane with gibberellins increases yield by increasing
practice_mcq.explanation: GA increases stem length, and sugarcane stores sugar in its stem, raising yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre.

practice_mcq.q: The rise in respiration rate during fruit ripening caused by ethylene is called
practice_mcq.explanation: Ethylene enhances the respiration rate during ripening; NCERT calls this rise the respiratory climactic.

practice_mcq.q: Ethylene promotes rapid internode and petiole elongation in
practice_mcq.explanation: In deep-water rice, ethylene-driven elongation keeps the leaves and upper shoot above water; bolting of rosette plants is a gibberellin effect.

practice_mcq.q: Which PGR is largely an inhibitor of growth activities although it could fit either group?
practice_mcq.explanation: NCERT states that the gaseous PGR ethylene could fit either group but is largely an inhibitor of growth activities.

practice_mcq.q: Ethephon is used in agriculture because it
options: is a synthetic auxin that kills weeds
practice_mcq.explanation: Ethephon in aqueous solution is absorbed and transported within the plant and releases ethylene slowly; it ripens tomatoes and apples and thins cotton, cherry and walnut.

options: It induces seed dormancy and desiccation tolerance
It acts as an antagonist of gibberellins
practice_mcq.explanation: ABA inhibits seed germination; the other three statements are NCERT facts.

practice_mcq.explanation: NCERT's example of open differentiation: cells away from the meristem become root cap, cells pushed to the periphery mature as epidermis.

common_mistakes: Defining growth as merely 'increase in size'. The examiner expects 'irreversible permanent increase in size accompanied by metabolic processes'; a seed swelling in water is not growth.

Swapping the discoveries: writing canary grass for Went or oat for Darwin, or naming Kurosawa for cytokinin. Darwin (canary grass), Went (oat), Kurosawa (rice, bakanae), Skoog and Miller (kinetin, herring sperm DNA), Cousins (oranges and bananas).
Attributing apical dominance to cytokinin. Auxin from the apical bud causes apical dominance; cytokinin overcomes it. In Assertion-Reason items this swap is the standard trap.
Writing that ABA ripens fruit or that ethylene closes stomata. Ethylene ripens; ABA closes stomata and is the stress hormone.

Confusing arithmetic and geometric growth at the cell level. Arithmetic: one daughter cell divides, the other differentiates; geometric: both keep dividing. Students often give only the graph shape and lose the cell-level mark.

Giving the wrong plasticity examples or the wrong reason. Cotton, coriander and larkspur show heterophylly with phase of life; buttercup shows it with environment (air versus water). 'Lotus' and 'water hyacinth' are not in NCERT and earn nothing.

Classifying kinetin as a carotenoid derivative or ABA as an adenine derivative. Kinetin is N<sup>6</sup>-furfurylamino purine (adenine derivative); ABA is derived from carotenoids; GA<sub>3</sub> is a terpene; IAA is an indole.

Forgetting the second half of the auxin sentence on abscission: auxin prevents early leaf and fruit drop but promotes abscission of old leaves and fruits. Writing only one half is marked as incomplete.
Quoting numbers wrongly: 17,500 cells per hour (maize root apex), 3,50,000 times (watermelon cell size), 20 tonnes per acre (sugarcane with GA). Wrong units or wrong plant lose the 1 mark.
strategy:
This chapter rewards precise recall more than understanding, so prepare it in two halves. The first half (growth, phases, growth rates, differentiation, development) is conceptual: learn the eight definitions of exercise question 1 in NCERT words, practise drawing the root tip with its three zones and the two growth graphs, and be able to work a small numerical on arithmetic growth and on absolute versus relative growth (the two-leaf example). Write the equations Lt = L0 + rt and W1 = W0ert with every symbol explained. Attach an example to each of differentiation, dedifferentiation and redifferentiation, and learn the four plasticity plants.

The second half (PGRs) is a table you must own. Make one table with five rows (auxin, GA, cytokinin, ethylene, ABA) and five columns: chemical class, discoverer and material, natural and synthetic examples, physiological effects in NCERT order, agricultural uses with the named crop (pineapple, tomato, 2,4-D lawns, grape, apple, sugarcane, conifer, cabbage, peanut, potato, deep-water rice, mango, cucumber, cotton, cherry, walnut). Revise this table daily for a week; nearly every MCQ, Assertion-Reason and 5-mark question comes from it. Then answer NCERT exercise questions 7 and 8 from memory, since they are the most-repeated school questions.

In the exam, give definitions with examples, give effects as numbered lists with the named crop, and add a labelled sketch wherever growth curves or the root tip are involved. Budget about 25 minutes for this chapter in a three-hour paper, and do the PGR table questions first because they are quick to write and quick to score.
revision_checklist: I can define growth in NCERT words and say why plant growth is indeterminate and open.
I can name the three meristems and link them to primary and secondary growth.
I can list the six parameters of growth and quote the maize (17,500 per hour), watermelon (3,50,000 times), pollen tube and leaf examples.
I can describe the meristematic, elongation and maturation phases with the features of cells in each and draw the root tip.

I can explain arithmetic and geometric growth at the cell level, write L<sub>t</sub> = L<sub>0</sub> + rt and W<sub>1</sub> = W<sub>0</sub>e<sup>rt</sup>, and draw the linear and sigmoid curves with lag, log and stationary phases.
I can distinguish absolute and relative growth rate with the two-leaf example and do a simple calculation.
I can list the conditions for growth with the role of each, including turgidity.
I can define differentiation, dedifferentiation and redifferentiation with the tracheary element, interfascicular cambium, cork cambium and secondary xylem examples.
I can explain why both growth and differentiation are open, with the root cap and epidermis example.
I can define development and plasticity and name cotton, coriander, larkspur and buttercup with the right reason for each.
I can state the chemical class of each PGR and split them into promoters and inhibitors.
I can tell the discovery story of all five PGRs with the scientist and the plant or material.
I can write the physiological effects and agricultural uses of auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins, ethylene and ABA with the named crops.
I can answer NCERT exercise questions 7 and 8 (which PGR for which job; what happens if) without looking.
I can explain apical dominance, bolting, parthenocarpy, respiratory climactic and why ABA is the stress hormone in one line each.
